questions.q: What is an Azure storage account?
options: The top-level namespace that holds blob, file, queue, and table storage underneath it
A single blob container and nothing else
A virtual machine's operating system disk
A billing-only label with no real resource behind it
questions.explain: Blob containers, file shares, queues, and tables are all created inside a storage account, which is the shared namespace and billing/management boundary.

questions.q: Why does an Azure storage account name have to be globally unique?
options: Because it becomes part of the account's public endpoint URL, e.g. https://<name>.blob.core.windows.net
Because Azure only allows one storage account per subscription
Because the name determines the performance tier automatically
Storage account names don't actually need to be unique
questions.explain: The account name is embedded in the public DNS endpoint, so it must be unique across all of Azure, not just your subscription.

questions.q: What's the main practical difference between the Standard and Premium performance tiers?
options: Standard is HDD-class and lower cost; Premium is SSD-class with low, consistent latency and higher IOPS
Standard only supports blob storage; Premium only supports file storage
Premium is always cheaper than Standard
There is no functional difference, only the name
questions.explain: Standard trades latency for lower cost on bulk unstructured data; Premium costs more but delivers low, consistent latency for demanding workloads.

questions.q: Which workload is the best fit for a Premium-tier storage resource?
options: A VM's OS disk or a latency-sensitive database workload mounted over SMB
A folder of monthly log archives nobody reads
Thirty-day-old backup files kept only for compliance
A static website's rarely-updated image assets
questions.explain: Premium's SSD-backed low latency matters for VM disks and latency-sensitive workloads; backups and archives are a better fit for Standard.

questions.q: What does the StorageV2 account kind support?
options: Blob, file, queue, and table storage together, on either the Standard or Premium tier
Only blob storage, never file shares
Only Premium-tier accounts
Legacy accounts that cannot be created anymore
questions.explain: General-purpose v2 (StorageV2) is the modern default kind and supports all four storage services on either performance tier.
